paper_title: Millimeter-wave WISP search with coherent Light-Shining-Through-a-Wall towards the STAX project
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing chi, dimensionless, as plotted on y-axis
notes: This is a proposal/proof-of-principle paper for a millimeter-wave (30 GHz) LSW dark photon search toward the STAX project. No new measured exclusion limit is presented; only projected sensitivities (Stages A, B, C at 2-sigma) shown in Figs. 6-7, which are not tabulated numerically. The only explicit numerical sensitivity in the text is for the low-power Stage A: 'one can address the chi ~ 1e-8 region around m_gamma' ~ 1e-4 eV'. The two emitted points approximately span the stated Stage A reach near 1e-4 eV (30 GHz corresponds to 1.24e-4 eV); this is a rough encoding, not a digitized curve. The paper targets the 1e-4 to 1e-3 eV mass range overall. LSW technique, so no local DM density assumption. Experimental work reported (coherency validation at 30 GHz) is instrumentation, not a physics limit. | [VISION GATE D] vision notes admit tracing a compilation envelope ('envelope of this work's constraints') rather than the paper's own single curve | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 7 of the paper (fig_06.png) shows projected 2-sigma exclusion limits of the proposed millimeter-wave coherent LSW experiment (STAX) in kinetic mixing chi vs dark photon mass. Three stages are shown: Stage A (low-power, floor ~2e-8), Stage B (high-power gyrotron, floor ~3e-9), and Stage C (single-photon detector + 1 MW gyrotron, floor ~3e-10). I traced Stage C, the deepest projected boundary (lower envelope of this work's constraints). These are PROJECTED sensitivities, not measured exclusions. LSW technique, so no dark matter density assumption is needed. The chi ~ m^-2 slope at low mass and resonance bumps (sin^4 structure, mitigated by combining resonator lengths L=180,200,220 mm) are reproduced. Spiky structures near 3-5e-4 eV read approximately. | Calibration: No calibration needed (spot-check verify/stage2 raw_ratio=0.97 snapped to identity)
